subject: English
passage:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• Habitat-based analysis and species-based analysis are two approaches in conservation biology.
• Habitat-based analysis examines how the physical features of an ecosystem support overall biodiversity.
• Nathan Quinn's habitat-based analysis of the Okavango Delta considered how seasonal flooding creates varied wetland zones that sustain a wide range of species.
• Species-based analysis focuses on the population dynamics of individual organisms.
• Jing Desai's species-based analysis of the Galápagos marine iguana tracked how declining algae supplies led to shrinking body sizes during El Niño years.
prompt: The student wants to present species-based analysis to an audience unfamiliar with the concept. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?

choices.A: An approach in conservation biology, species-based analysis focuses on the population dynamics of individual organisms.
choices.B: A habitat-based analysis of the Okavango Delta might consider how seasonal flooding creates varied wetland zones that sustain a wide range of species.
choices.C: Habitat-based analysis differs from species-based analysis in that habitat-based analysis examines how the physical features of an ecosystem support overall biodiversity.
choices.D: A study of the Galápagos marine iguana showed how declining algae supplies led to shrinking body sizes during El Niño years.

explanation:
Choice A is the best answer. The sentence effectively presents species-based analysis to an unfamiliar audience by identifying it as an approach in conservation biology and explaining that it focuses on the population dynamics of individual organisms.

Why B is incorrect:

Choice B is incorrect. The sentence describes a habitat-based analysis of the Okavango Delta; it doesn't present species-based analysis to an unfamiliar audience.
